Authorized two-host acceptance harness only. HTTPS uses an explicit CA certificate and hostname verification; FTP uses AUTH TLS with encrypted data, and Telnet uses verified TLS. Public listener binds are necessary for the physical exchange. Random test accounts, isolated per-user roots and negative guest/path checks are exercised; no credentials are published.

Owner selects an HTTPS bootstrap URL; download is bounded to 256 MiB and verified against the required expected SHA-256 before any archive extraction or native execution. This is a deployment CLI, not a remote user supplied URL fetch service.

Owner deployment CLI intentionally binds public extension protocols to all interfaces; public authenticated FTP and Telnet require TLS, SSH uses SFTP with no shell, and unauthenticated Gopher is isolated to a separate public root. Credentials remain in the existing private native configuration.

Owner selects an HTTPS bootstrap URL; download is bounded to 256 MiB and verified against the required expected SHA-256 before any archive extraction or native execution. This is a deployment CLI, not a remote user supplied URL fetch service.

Owner invokes a CLI with an HTTPS gateway origin; only the domain-bound signed public naming transaction is transmitted. TLS certificate verification remains enabled, request timeout is 30 seconds, and no local secrets are included in the payload.

Telnet is a required UFS extension. Public authenticated sessions require TLS; plaintext requires an explicit owner opt-in for an encrypted tunnel. Each session is authenticated and confined to its account file root, with a fixed UFS command set and no operating system shell.

The wildcard bind address is normalized to localhost only for the fixed owner-configured loopback status client. Status uses SHA-256 Digest credentials from a private file, disallows redirects and proxies, verifies TLS if enabled, and bounds the response to 64 KiB.

archival_findings: Legacy originals include unsafe eval/pickle/shell and obsolete algorithms. They remain historical text source and are absent from ziokt.pyz/openci.pyz and activated application profiles. Active compatibility readers use restricted deserialization; this report does not certify historical originals for execution.
